subject: Optimize: pipeline indexing, parallel search, two-pass semantic retrieval

claude.title: Pipeline parallelism exploits Claude API as the bottleneck, not embeddings
claude.body: Claude takes ~5s per batch while embedding takes ~50ms, making them a natural pipeline pair. Background threading overlaps embedding of batch N with Claude processing of batch N+1. Semantic search uses a two-pass strategy: first score all embeddings using only (id, embedding) pairs to avoid deserializing JSON and allocating strings, then load full rows only for top-N results. This is critical as the index grows — skipping deserialization for discarded rows saves significant allocation pressure.

parsed.title: Overlapping I/O and CPU-bound work via background threading in retrieval pipeline
parsed.body: The system identified that LLM processing was the primary latency bottleneck (~5s) compared to embedding generation (~50ms). By moving embedding generation into a background thread, the pipeline now overlaps these operations, effectively hiding the fast embedding cost behind the slow LLM inference. This pattern is also applied to search queries where embedding generation runs concurrently with context setup.

parsed.title: Two-pass semantic search to minimize deserialization overhead
parsed.body: The original implementation loaded full database rows including JSON-serialized fields for all candidates before filtering by similarity. The optimized approach uses a two-pass strategy: first computing cosine similarity on raw embedding bytes and IDs, then fetching full row details only for the top-N results. This significantly reduces memory allocation and CPU time spent deserializing data that would ultimately be discarded.

The key architectural insight is that init/uninit now have a side effect beyond the local repo — they register globally, turning diwa from a per-repo tool into one that manages a fleet. subject: 0.3.5: idempotent indexing, stale hook cleanup, hook logging

claude.title: Idempotent indexing prevents duplicate insights on re-runs
claude.body: The `diwa index` command was made idempotent by querying existing commit SHAs before processing. This means rerunning the indexer fills gaps from failed or partial runs without duplicating already-processed commits. The approach uses a simple SET lookup of indexed SHAs rather than upsert logic, keeping the insert path clean while making the skip decision at the orchestration layer.

claude.title: Stale git hooks left behind when core.hooksPath diverges from .git/hooks
claude.body: When a repo uses a custom hooks path (e.g. Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky), the diwa post-commit hook could be installed in .git/hooks but never fire because git reads from the configured path instead. The fix detects when the active hooks directory differs from .git/hooks and cleans up the stale hook from the inactive location, preventing silent failures where commits appear to go unindexed.

claude.title: Silent hook failures are undiagnosable without logging
claude.body: The post-commit hook previously redirected output to /dev/null, making it impossible to diagnose why indexing silently failed after a commit. Switching to a dedicated log file (~/.diwa/hooks.log) preserves the fire-and-forget behavior that hooks need while giving users a trail to follow when things break. This is a common pattern for background processes triggered by git hooks.

claude.title: Hook re-install overwrites instead of no-oping to propagate improvements
claude.body: Previously install_hook would skip installation if a hook file already existed, meaning users who upgraded diwa would keep running the old hook script indefinitely. Changing to an overwrite-on-reinstall strategy ensures that `diwa update` propagates hook script improvements like the logging change. This trades the safety of never touching an existing hook for the practical need to evolve the hook over time.

parsed.title: Implementing idempotency in indexing pipelines via pre-checks
parsed.body: The commit introduces a mechanism to skip commits that already have insights, making the `diwa index` command idempotent. This architectural decision ensures that re-running the indexer fills gaps without duplicating data, which is crucial for robustness in automated or repeated CI/CD contexts.

parsed.title: Handling custom git hook paths to prevent stale installations
parsed.body: A bug was fixed where the tool failed to clean up hooks if `core.hooksPath` pointed to a different location (e.g., `.husky`) than the default `.git/hooks`. The fix ensures that when the active hook path differs from the installed location, the inactive hook is removed. This prevents stale hooks from lingering and causing unexpected behavior or conflicts.

parsed.title: Enabling diagnosability by logging hook execution to a persistent file
parsed.body: The decision was made to change hook logging from `/dev/null` to `~/.diwa/hooks.log`. This allows developers to diagnose failures that occur within the git hook context, where stdout/stderr might be suppressed or lost. It shifts the tooling philosophy from 'fire and forget' to observable operations.

parsed.title: Re-installation logic must update existing artifacts rather than no-op
parsed.body: The `install_hook` function was previously a no-op if the hook already existed. This was changed to update the script on re-install. The learning here is that 'update' commands must propagate changes to already-installed components; otherwise, users will run outdated logic even after upgrading the main binary.

subject: 0.4.0: push-based indexing via daemon + queue, post-merge hooks

claude.title: Push-based indexing via daemon eliminates hook latency and catches missed commits
claude.body: Switched from synchronous in-hook indexing to an async model where hooks drop flag files into a queue directory and a launchd daemon processes them in the background. This solved two problems: hook latency (enqueue doesn't load the ORT model, keeping hooks sub-10ms) and naturally debounces bursty activity like git pull landing many commits. Also discovered that fast-forward pulls via post-merge hooks were never being indexed — this explained why katulong had 133 unindexed commits.

parsed.title: Shift from synchronous hook processing to push-based daemon indexing
parsed.body: The system migrated from executing indexing logic directly within git hooks to a decoupled architecture where hooks only enqueue files into a local directory watched by a launchd-managed daemon. This design decision prioritizes sub-10ms hook latency by avoiding heavy dependencies (like ORT) during the hook execution phase, while naturally debouncing bursty activities such as large git pulls.
parsed.tags: architecture daemon indexing latency decoupling launchd

parsed.title: Resolve missed indexing for fast-forward merges via post-merge hooks
parsed.body: A critical gap was identified where fast-forward pulls did not trigger the previous hook logic, leading to significant unindexed commit backlogs (e.g., 133 commits in a single repo). The fix involved installing post-merge hooks alongside existing ones to ensure that all merge strategies, including fast-forwards, are captured and indexed correctly.
parsed.tags: bugfix git-hooks fast-forward merge indexing gap

parsed.title: Implement idempotent auto-migration for existing users in package post-install
parsed.body: To seamlessly transition existing users to the new daemon-based model, a `diwa migrate` command was integrated into the Homebrew `post_install` hook. This process rewrites hooks in all registered repositories and loads the daemon agent without touching existing indexed data. The migration is designed to be idempotent and non-blocking; if it fails during install, it logs a warning and relies on a lazy auto-migration trigger on the next tool invocation.

subject: feat: tunnels heal command (#1)

claude.title: KeepAlive must be unconditional or launchd won't restart after graceful shutdown
claude.body: The root cause was that KeepAlive with SuccessfulExit=false meant launchd would not restart cloudflared after a SIGTERM (exit 0). Changing to unconditional KeepAlive=true fixed tunnel recovery. Additionally, the heal command needed to handle tunnels that are loaded but have no running process (pid: None), which is the exact state after a graceful shutdown that launchd failed to restart. This is a subtle launchd behavior that's easy to get wrong.

claude.title: Replace string sentinel parsing with structured fields for status checks
claude.body: Connection status was originally checked via string matching (`connections.starts_with("no ")`) which is fragile and error-prone. Refactored to a `connection_count: usize` field on TunnelInfo, making status checks numeric comparisons instead of string parsing. This eliminated a class of bugs where display-oriented strings were being used for logic decisions across multiple call sites (cli_heal, app.rs service status).

claude.title: Heal command defaults to healthy when API data is missing to avoid false-positive restarts
claude.body: When the Cloudflare API is unreachable or returns incomplete data, the heal command assumes tunnels are healthy (unwrap_or(true) instead of false). This prevents false-positive restarts that could cause unnecessary disruption. The command also bails entirely if tunnel_info is empty, distinguishing between 'all tunnels healthy' and 'attempted healing but everything failed' in its summary output.

parsed.title: Unconditional KeepAlive required for launchd to restart gracefully exited processes
parsed.body: The initial implementation used `KeepAlive=SuccessfulExit=false`, which prevented launchd from restarting the `cloudflared` process after a graceful shutdown (SIGTERM resulting in exit code 0). This left tunnels in a 'loaded but not running' state. The fix changed this to an unconditional `KeepAlive=true` and updated the heal logic to specifically target tunnels with no active PID, ensuring recovery from this specific failure mode.

parsed.title: Replace string sentinel parsing with structured connection count for health checks
parsed.body: The system previously relied on checking if a connection string started with 'no ' to determine tunnel status, which was fragile and prone to false positives. This commit introduces a `connection_count` field to the `TunnelInfo` struct, allowing for deterministic integer comparisons (`> 0`) instead of string matching. This improves the reliability of the heal command and status displays by removing dependency on specific API response formatting.

parsed.title: Default to healthy state when API data is missing to prevent false-positive restarts
parsed.body: During the implementation of the heal command, it was determined that transient API failures or missing data should not trigger unnecessary tunnel restarts. The logic was updated to use `unwrap_or(true)` for health checks and explicitly bail out if tunnel info is empty. This 'fail-open' strategy ensures that network glitches in the monitoring layer do not cause disruption to the actual tunnels.

subject: fix restart not picking up updated tokens, improve token edit UX

claude.title: launchctl kickstart -k reuses cached plist, defeating token updates
claude.body: restart() used launchctl kickstart -k which reuses the cached service definition, so plist changes (like updated tunnel tokens) were silently ignored. The fix switches to a full bootout + bootstrap cycle to force launchd to reload the plist. This is a macOS launchd subtlety: kickstart is fast but stale, stop+start is correct when the plist has changed.

claude.title: Allow bare token argument when only one tunnel exists
claude.body: token edit now accepts a bare token (tunnels token edit eyJ...) without --token flag when only one tunnel is configured. This reduces friction for the common single-tunnel setup while keeping the explicit flag available for multi-tunnel disambiguation. The ergonomic shortcut was paired with the restart fix since both improve the token-update workflow end to end.

parsed.title: Use full stop/start cycle instead of kickstart to ensure plist changes are loaded
parsed.body: The previous restart logic used `launchctl kickstart -k`, which reuses the cached service definition and fails to pick up changes to the plist file, such as updated tunnel tokens. To resolve this, the implementation was changed to always perform a full stop (bootout) and start (bootstrap) cycle. This ensures that the launchd daemon reloads the modified configuration file from disk before starting the service.

parsed.title: Simplify CLI interface by allowing positional arguments for single-resource operations
parsed.body: The token editing UX was improved to accept a bare token as a positional argument when only one tunnel is configured. This removes the friction of requiring a `--token` flag in common single-resource scenarios while maintaining explicit naming requirements for multi-resource setups. The change includes validation logic to ensure the specified name matches an existing tunnel, preventing accidental updates to the wrong configuration.

claude.title: Route import designed as pure parse/retarget layer with idempotent API calls
claude.body: The route import feature was deliberately split into pure logic (route_import.rs) and side-effectful CLI glue (main.rs). The pure module handles parsing, retargeting routes to a different tunnel, and grouping by tunnel — all covered by 11 unit tests. Actual Cloudflare mutations reuse the existing idempotent add_route path, so re-running an import is safe. This separation makes the cross-tunnel move workflow (pipe from one tunnel, import to another) composable via Unix pipes.

subject: v0.10.1: actually include the launchd Intel-mac + stop-reap fix

claude.title: Hardcoded Homebrew path breaks Intel Macs — resolve cloudflared at plist-write time
claude.body: The plist generator hardcoded /opt/homebrew/bin/cloudflared, which only exists on Apple Silicon. Intel Macs use /usr/local/bin, causing silent exit-78 failures. The fix introduces a cloudflared_path() resolver that checks env override, both Homebrew prefixes, then falls back to `which`. This is a classic cross-architecture portability lesson: never hardcode platform-specific package manager paths.

claude.title: stop() must reap child process before reporting success — prevents secret leakage
claude.body: The previous stop() called launchctl unload and returned immediately, but cloudflared could still be alive holding tunnel credentials. The fix snapshots the PID before unloading, polls for child exit for 3 seconds, then SIGKILLs as a last resort. This matters for security: reporting 'stopped' while the process still holds secrets is a correctness bug with real consequences.

claude.title: Unstaged changes in working tree silently missed during bulk-copy release workflow
claude.body: v0.10.0 was supposed to include the launchd fixes, but the bulk-copy during release grabbed the committed version of launchd.rs while the actual fix sat unstaged in the working tree. This required a v0.10.1 patch release. The lesson: when cutting releases that pull from another branch, verify working tree cleanliness or stage everything first — committed state and working-tree state are easy to conflate.

parsed.title: Resolve cloudflared path dynamically to support both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs
parsed.body: Hardcoding the cloudflared binary path to `/opt/homebrew` caused silent failures on Intel Macs where Homebrew installs to `/usr/local`. The fix implements a multi-step resolution strategy that checks environment variables, standard Homebrew paths for both architectures, and the system PATH before falling back to a default. This ensures the launchd plist is generated with a valid binary path regardless of the user's hardware architecture.
parsed.tags: macos launchd homebrew path-resolution apple-silicon intel

parsed.title: Implement robust process termination with PID snapshotting and timeout-based SIGKILL
parsed.body: The previous stop mechanism returned success immediately after unloading the launchd service, leaving the cloudflared process alive and holding sensitive secrets. The new implementation snapshots the PID before unloading, polls for child exit for 3 seconds, and only sends SIGKILL if the process is still running. This prevents a race condition where the application appears stopped but the underlying tunnel remains active.

parsed.title: Verify working tree state before bulk-copying files between branches
parsed.body: Version 0.10.0 was released with a bug because the developer copied `launchd.rs` from the main branch without realizing the critical fix existed only in the unstaged working tree, not in the committed history. This highlights the importance of checking `git status` and ensuring all intended changes are committed before performing cross-branch file operations to avoid shipping incomplete features.
